title: natsel architecture
description: From genes in code to species at the edge and back through events

children.title: Skills
children.details:
Wrap every change as a gene.

LLM skills act as codemods that follow the **gene contract**: one locus, dependencies only through nesting (a gene inside another gene), mechanical removal.

- **create** a gene with several alleles
- **delete** a losing gene (a PR)
- **fix** a winning gene: merge into the base and remove the flag (a PR)

A human approves every PR.

children.title: Registration
children.details:
SDK sends the gene list to the Control Plane.

At build time the SDK collects the list of genes and sends it to the Control Plane. **Code is the source of truth**: a gene exists only if it is in the code. Each nested gene is sent with its parent.

children.title: Registry
children.details:
Assigns each gene a position in dna.

Positions of extinct genes are not reused while old cookies live; a new epoch starts with a new `dna` version.

The registry also keeps the **nesting tree**: which gene lives inside which.

children.title: Species
children.details:
Assembles species from suitable genes.

Composes only valid genotypes: a nested gene is switched on only together with its parent. Genotypes that differ only in genes hidden by an off parent count as one species.

Every new species passes an automated **smoke test** and an optional **manual approval** before it gets traffic.

children.title: Weights
children.details:
Thompson sampling by niches, under constraints.

Traffic weights come from species metrics. Manual control is expressed as **constraints** (max share, ramp-up, segments, forbidden combinations), never as weight edits, so the statistics stay valid.

children.title: Statistics
children.details:
Regression of gene contributions.

Fitness is scored **per gene**, by regression over species genotypes. Interactions are modelled within a locus. A nested gene is scored only on users whose parent gene is on. Low score → extinction, consistent win → fixation.

children.title: Cleanup
children.details:
Codemod for extinct genes, no AI.

For every gene where selection is over, a **deterministic codemod** (no AI) replaces the flag check with the winning allele's branch, deletes the losing branches and opens a merge request. The owning team reviews and merges it; the gene leaves the pool on the next CI scan.

blocks.title: Breeder
blocks.details:
Picks a species for each user.

Sits in front of the CDN and takes weights from the Control Plane. **Hash mode** (default, nothing stored on the device): the species comes from HMAC(daily salt, IP + User-Agent) by weighted rendezvous hashing, stable for a day; extinction moves only the extinct species' users. **Cookie mode**: `dna` goes to a cookie and a returning user keeps their species until it goes extinct.

`dna` is a signed (HMAC) bit record: `version | gene field 1 | gene field 2 | …`. A bad signature means reassignment. Hundreds of genes fit in tens of bytes.

blocks.title: CDN and app
blocks.details:
dna in the cache key; SDK enables genes.

The CDN includes `dna` in the cache key, so the cache splits by the number of species, not users.

The SDK makes no requests at runtime: it enables genes from `dna`. Unknown bits are ignored and a gene without a bit runs its default, so rolling back a build is safe.

blocks.title: Events
blocks.details:
Exposures, outcomes, fast guardrail.

Exposures (`dna` + the gene that actually fired) and outcome events, on top of your existing analytics (warehouse-native). A **fast guardrail path** kills a lethal species within minutes.
